newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FORTIS SAYS WANTS 75% OF CGER.
newsitem.headline: FORTIS SAYS WANTS 75% OF CGER.

text.p: Belgian-Dutch bancasssurance group Fortis would be "happy" to raise its stake in Belgian ASLK/CGER's banking and insurance operations to 75 percent from 49.9 percent currently, newspapers on Friday quoted Fortis AG chairman Maurice Lippens as saying.
The Belgian state is in the process of fully privatising CGER. It wants to reduce its CGER stake to about 25 percent from the 49.9 percent it now holds, and has said it favours a bourse listing.
The government is currently in talks with Fortis, which has the right of first refusal on the CGER shares to be sold.
Lippens did not rule out a bourse listing, however.
"We are takers for the 25 percent up for sale," he said. But "we are not prejudging (the situation) if it can be proven to us that (a bourse listing) is the best solution for CGER."

Lippens was quoted in at least two Belgian papers, Le Soir and L'Echo, as saying that if 10 percent of CGER were listed on the stock exchange, it would be much more difficult for the state to get a non-discounted price for its stake.

Considering discounts of eight percent set by Generale Bank on shares in last year's capital increase and of 12 percent set by Fortis when it last tapped the markets, the state would have to offer future CGER shareholders a discount to intrinsic share value of more than eight percent, Lippens added.
He said he was happy for the state to keep a 25.1 percent stake in CGER, adding that it was "a good partner".
